title: Products of integral varieties over an algebraically closed field
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty integral schemes [def-pc-integral-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Then their scheme fibre product $A\times_k B$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is integral. Here separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion, and integral means reduced and irreducible. No smoothness, normality or properness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05P3, lemma-product-varieties, statement and affine tensor-product proof, lines 85--141.

proof.text: By finite type, choose finite affine open covers $A=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ and $B=\bigcup_{j\in J}V_j$, writing $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}R_i$ and $V_j=\operatorname{Spec}S_j$, with each coordinate algebra finitely generated over $k$. Discard empty members. Since $A,B$ are nonempty, $I,J$ are nonempty. By the definition of integrality every $R_i,S_j$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 05P3, lemma-product-varieties, first paragraph of the proof: finite affine covers and reduction to the affine case

proof.text: Put $P=A\times_kB$ with projections $p,q$. Base-changing the open inclusions first along $p$ and then along the projection to $B$ identifies $W_{ij}=U_i\times_kV_j$ with an open subscheme of $P$. More explicitly this open is $p^{-1}(U_i)\cap q^{-1}(V_j)$: a morphism to $P$ factors through it exactly when its two components factor through $U_i$ and $V_j$, which is precisely the fibre-product universal property. Thus the $W_{ij}$ cover $P$, since the $U_i,V_j$ cover the factors. The affine fibre-product formula gives $W_{ij}\cong\operatorname{Spec}(R_i\otimes_kS_j)$. Apply the existing tensor-domain lemma: $k$ is algebraically closed, $R_i$ is a domain, and $S_j$ is a finite-type domain. Hence every chart ring $R_i\otimes_kS_j$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 05P3, lemma-product-varieties, affine reduction and tensor-domain argument; affine formula: schemes.tex Tag 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes; openness: Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion

proof.text: For any $(i,j),(i\prime,j\prime)$, put $U=U_i\cap U_{i\prime}$ and $V=V_j\cap V_{j\prime}$. Both are nonempty: the factors are irreducible by integrality, and two disjoint nonempty opens would express an irreducible space as the union of their two proper closed complements. The structure map $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is surjective because the target has one point. Surjectivity is stable under base change, so $U\times_kV\to V$ is surjective. As $V$ is nonempty, $U\times_kV$ is nonempty. By the inverse-image description in step 2 and the fibre-product universal property, $U\times_kV$ is the open intersection $W_{ij}\cap W_{i\prime j\prime}$. Thus every pair of product charts meets. No claim that the underlying space of a scheme product is the Cartesian product of its underlying spaces is needed.

source.place: Tag 05P3, lemma-product-varieties, justification of the pairwise-overlap hypothesis in the affine reduction; properties.tex Tag 01OM, lemma-characterize-irreducible; morphisms.tex Tag 01S1, lemma-base-change-surjective

proof.text: The family $(W_{ij})_{(i,j)\in I\times J}$ is an affine open cover of $P$, with nonempty index set, domain coordinate rings by step 2, and pairwise nonempty intersections by step 3. These are exactly the hypotheses of the integral affine-cover criterion. It follows that $P=A\times_kB$ is integral, as claimed.
